pages.name: Space Combat Procedure
pages.html:
Space Combat Procedure

1) Determine Initiative: Each ship rolls initiative: Roll 1D and add the ship’s M-Drive rating along with the pilot’s Pilot Skill rank. The ship with the highest roll acts first. Any time identical results occur, both act simultaneously.

2) Determine Crew Positions: Crew members choose which crew positions they would like to be in. Crew members may choose to change positions from the prior round.

  • Crew members with multiple positions incur -2DM to any check per position they are fulfilling. The ship computer can help offset this.

3) Main Combat Step: Each ship acts on their turn, based on initiative, and resolves the following orders.

  • Movement: Allocate thrust to change range band. Any unused thrust can be used defensively this round.
  • Fire turret: Apply distance DM to any turret attacks.
  • Fire beam: Apply distance DM to any beam attacks.
  • Fire missiles: Missiles take a number of rounds to reach their target equal to the range band distance. Missiles are homing and automatically hit unless the targeted ship successfully evades.
  • Fire countermeasures: Use sandcasters to apply penalties to a single target.
  • Determine additional crew actions: Any crew member who didn’t act may perform one action based on their position.

4) Missile Resolution: Once all ships act, determine if any missiles fired in previous rounds hit.

  • Defending ship gunners can attempt to shoot incoming missiles if they didn't act this round.
  • Defending ship pilot rolls pilot skill to avoid, but may add any unused thrust from this round to assist.

5) Determine Crew Morale: If a ship has been damaged by 50%, the referee makes a morale check for the NPC crew members and passengers to see if they keep their cool.

  • Captain: The captain can make a leadership check, where the effect of the roll is added to the morale check.
  • Failure: The crew members incur -2DM to all future skill checks during the combat.

6) Determine if Dogfighting Occurs: If two ships end up in adjacent range, both ships' gunners take turns firing volleys at each other, including using any fixed mounted weapons if the ship was positioned towards the dogfighting ship during the round.

Once all ships have acted, return to step 1.

Book p.84

Book p.84

pages.name: Space Movement
pages.html:
Space Movement

Space Movement: To change range bands, a ship needs to spend a number of rounds equal to the desired range while using thrust equal to the range bands.

  • For example: if a ship with a M-2 drive wants to move two range bands, then they have to spend two 10-minute rounds using 2 thrust.

Book p.84

pages.name: Starship Combat Rounds and Dogfighting
pages.html:
Starship Combat Rounds

Starship Combat Rounds: Starship combat rounds are 10-minutes.

Dogfighting

  • Dogfighting: Starships that end up within adjacent ranges on the same round are considered to be “dogfighting.” The normal combat procedure is followed. At the end of the space combat round, one additional volley of combat actions happens between the gunners of each ship as determined by the round’s initiative.
  • Any unused thrust from the prior starship combat round can allow the pilot to evade, only during dogfighting. At the end of a dogfight, the two ships are considered to be in Close distance range.
  • Example: Starship A had higher initiative than Starship B. The space combat round happens as normal, but the ships end up adjacent to each other, indicating dogfighting. Ship A’s gunners attack once followed by Ship B’s gunners. After this happens, the ships drift out of range into close distance, finishing the round.

Book p.84

pages.name: Additional Crew Actions by Position
pages.html:
Additional Crew Actions by Position

Additional Crew Actions: Any characters that haven’t acted yet may change ship positions and perform one of the following actions per round. All actions require an 8+ to succeed unless stated otherwise.

Technician: Use the Computer Skill to perform one of the following.

  • Change program: Change, run or install a new program module for next round.
  • Repair computer system: Attempt to repair computer damage, to restore bandwidth capabilities. On success, +1 bandwidth is restored.

Captain: Use Leadership Skill for the rally action or Tactics Skill for the tactics action.

  • Rally: reroll leadership to remove any morale penalties. A success allows for the removal of any negative DM from morale, while a failure keeps the penalty. This can only be done a number of times equal to the captain’s leadership rank.
  • Command: Give orders to crew to perform a specific action to prepare for the next round.
  • Tactics: Make a Tactics roll and the effect of the roll can be allocated to any crew member next round to use on their check.

Pilot: Use Pilot Skill for the following. The pilot determines how much of the ship’s thrust is used when performing any of their tasks. Remember: thrust is determined by the ship’s M-Drive; so a M-Drive with 2 output creates 2 thrust.

  • Evade: This is performed only when being fired upon and can be performed as long as the ship has thrust to spend. Each evade attempt will use thrust, but the thrust used counts as +DM. The pilot can choose how much thrust to allot per turn. When a pilot evades, they add the effect of their roll as a -DM to the attacker firing at their ship.
  • Firing position: The pilot must position their ship to fire any fix-mounted weapons at a target. This action uses one thrust and doesn’t require a Skill roll.
  • Change range band: The pilot can automatically use thrust to change range bands, using the required amount of thrust needed per round.

Sensor Operator: Use Comms Skill to perform one of the following.

  • Jammer: If the ship has ECM installed in the computer, the sensor operator causes a target to incur a -2DM to ranged attacks until the next round. This action is automatic and may be maintained without needing to roll. However, the sensor operator may instead focus their jamming action on missiles or energy weapons from a target ship.
  • Jamming missiles: On a 8+ any incoming missiles detonate prematurely.
  • Jamming energy weapons: On a 8+, apply the sensor operator’s comms rank as a -DM to a target ship’s energy weapon attack rolls until the next round.
  • Scramble comms: Prevent target from communicating with allies, causing them to incur -2 morale. This penalty ends when the scrambling ends.

Engineer: Use Engineer Skill to perform one of the following.

  • Overload plant: This allows the ship’s power plant to function at a higher output above its current classification. 8+ succeeds at one step above, 10+ succeeds at two steps above, etc. On a failure, the power plant incurs damage equal to the failed effect.
  • Divert power: Decrease the quality of one system to temporarily increase the quality of another drive. A failure will damage both affected systems by -1. This allows a weapon to deal +1 more damage or the M-Drive to gain +1 thrust. The M or J-Drive cannot exceed the current POW rating unless the plant has been overloaded.

Astrogator: Use the Astrogation Skill to perform one of the following.

  • Emergency calculation: 12+ to calculate the nearest jump point. Each round spent decreases the difficulty by 1.
  • Activate jump drive: When a ship reaches its jump point, the astrogator initiates the jump, provided that the J-Drive rating can meet the jump destination.

Mechanic: Use Mechanic Skill to perform one of the following.

  • Repair: The mechanic can choose a damaged area to perform emergency repairs on. The mechanic incurs -1DM per damage the area has sustained. A successful repair allows for 1 hit to be restored and uses 1D repair parts.
  • Jury-rig: Temporarily fix a ship system to run at its normal classification, but with an increase in the difficulty to use it from 8+ to 10+.

Gunner: Use the Gunner Skill. Any time the gunner fires, apply any range DM. The target ship may apply a -DM due to it evading.

  • Use turret: A turret doesn’t need the ship to be positioned to be fired. 8+ is a hit.
  • Use fixed mounted weapon: The ship must be positioned toward a specific target to use fixed mounted weapons, as determined by the pilot. 8+ is a hit.
  • Select Target Location: -4DM for a gunner to attack a specific location on a starship.

Book p.84-85

pages.name: Other Actions
pages.html:
Other Actions

  • Put on vaccsuit: Any crew member not in a vaccsuit can spend one space combat round to put on a vaccsuit in case of emergency.
  • Depressurize cabin: A ship’s crew can intentionally depressurize their cabin to prevent explosive depressurization in the cabin. Depressurizing also allows them to vacuum-seal different areas from decompression, such as specific cargo containers or certain staterooms. Repressurizing the cabin takes two space combat rounds (20 minutes).
  • Reload missiles: Any crew member can reload the missiles into the missile tube if all the missiles were used.
  • First aid: A crew member can apply first aid to another crew member who was injured.
  • Assist: A crew member can assist one of the occupied crew positions as long as they have Rank 0 in the necessary Skill. Assisting provides +1DM to any rolls for that crew position, regardless of the assisting member's Skill rank.

Book p.85

1DSmall Craft Location

Any time a ship system takes damage, it decreases its capabilities by one step. Use the ship record sheet to track ship damage.

  • Remember: As M-Drives, J-Drives, and the power plant are damaged, they will decrease in classification and limit their potential output.
  • Critical condition: When a system is damaged to its lowest rating, the system is considered to be in critical condition and can only be repaired in a starport. For example, a 100t ship with a B rated M-Drive is damaged and is reduced to functioning as an A rated m-drive the lowest it could be- thus it is in critical condition. Please note: a ship that only operates with an installed system at its lowest capacity does not gain critical condition but is outright destroyed on a hit.
  • Called shots: A gunner can choose to attack a specific location on a target ship but will incur a -2DM.
  • Destroyed ship: When a ship is destroyed, it will explode on a roll of 4+ on 1D. Otherwise it will break apart, with its cargo and anyone in a vaccsuit adrift.

Book p.86

pages.name: Damage Location Effects
pages.html:
Damage Location Effects

Hull: The hull is the body of the ship, and more frequently hit. A hull can take a number of hits equal to 1 plus 1 per 100T.

  • Critical condition: When a ship’s hull reaches hull 1, it is considered in critical condition.
  • Destroyed: A ship with hull 0 is considered destroyed and breaks apart.

M-Drive: When the M-Drive takes damage, it decreases in class equal to the amount of damage. For example, if a C-Class M-Drive takes one damage, it is now considered B-Class. This may have an impact on the ships ability to maneuver, causing it to be less effective the more damage it receives.

  • Critical condition: When the M-Drive reaches its lowest rating, the M-Drive is considered in critical condition.
  • Destroyed: Any additional hits destroys the M-Drive beyond repair.

J-Drive: When a J-Drive takes damage, it decreases one step per damage taken, similar to the M-drive.

  • Critical condition: When the J-Drive is at its lowest rating, it is considered critical.
  • Destroyed: Any additional damage taken to the J-Drive permanently destroys the J-Drive beyond repair.

Power: When the power plant takes damage, it also decreases one step per damage received just like the M- and J-Drives. However, if the power plant’s quality decreases below that of the M- and J-Drives’ output, then those drives only function equal to what the power plant’s max is.

  • For example, if a power plant on a 100T ship drops from B-Class to A-Class, then the M- and J-drives can only function as A-Class.
  • Critical condition: When the power plant reaches its lowest rating, the plant is considered in critical condition.
  • Destroyed: Any additional hits destroy the power plant, causing the ship to explode.

Fuel: When a fuel leak happens, then the amount of usable fuel decreases by 10T per damage sustained.

  • For example, a ship with 30T of fuel allotted can take 3 hits to the fuel tank before it is empty.
  • J-Drive minimum: Keep in mind, different hulls and J-Drives use different amounts of fuel, so use the ship record sheet to note down the minimal amount of fuel needed to make a jump.
  • Critical condition: When the fuel reaches 0 hits, the ship runs out of fuel and requires the fuel tanks to be repaired before refuelling. Additional hits will count against the hull.

Internal: Internal represents damage to the life support system, cargo hold, and computer. The internal areas can sustain a number of hits equal to 1 per 100T. Anytime the internal area of the ship is hit, roll D3 to determine what is impacted:

  • 1) Computer: Every hit decreases the amount of programs capable of functioning by 1.
  • 2) Crew injury: All crew members on board attempt to roll 8+ to avoid damage, but add their END mod and any -1DM from the Internal damage. Anyone in a low berth needs a 8+ to avoid the berth shorting out, but even if it does, it can be repaired. Referees can choose to roll a D3 and apply it to all NPCs on board as automatic damage taken, to streamline resolution.
  • 3) Cargo hold: To determine if the cargo hold is damaged, roll 8+ to determine if damage was avoided. On a failed roll, the difference is multiplied by 10% to determine how much cargo was damaged. For example if a 6 was rolled then 20% of the cargo was damaged.
  • Critical condition: Once the Internal reaches 0 hits remaining, the interior depressurizes, causing immediate death to anyone not in a vaccsuit, due to the explosive depressurization. Any additional hit counts against the hull.

Weapon: If a weapon system is hit, it is inoperable until it is repaired.

  • Critical condition: Any additional hits to a weapon system destroys the weapon beyond repair and counts as damage against the hull.

Book p.86-87

pages.name: Abandon Ship
pages.html:
Abandon Ship

Abandon ship: When a starship is on the verge of exploding or has fallen apart and is not capable of operating, the crew should abandon ship.

  • Boarding a small craft: Boarding a small craft takes a crew 10 minutes per 100T of the ship to safely board with necessary supplies or last-minute items. Multiple small craft can reduce this amount.
  • Emergency evac: When a ship is destroyed in a space combat round, the crew has to board in under 10 minutes to flee on a small craft; otherwise they will perish with the ship if it explodes.
  • Vaccsuits: A spacer in a vaccsuit can survive drifting in the vacuum of space for 15 hours before running out of air. If the vaccsuit is equipped with an extra air tank, it will provide an additional 15 hours.
  • Reentry shell: Some vaccsuits may have an additional reentry pack installed, which deploys when beginning to free fall into the atmosphere to protect the spacer. The shell unfurls around the vaccsuit into a bubble-like membrane and absorbs the reentry friction and burns off. The pack will then deploy a parachute to aid with landing. The shell isn’t guaranteed to protect the spacer, and requires a 6+ roll modified by Vaccsuit skill to enter at ideal trajectory; otherwise the spacer will burn up regardless of the reentry shell.

Book p.87
